title: (No AI) Here’s the problem with putting an AI image generator in Google Earth
author: Stevie Bonifield
content:
![An AI-edited Google Earth image of a cabin in the mountains](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/07/Dream-House.mp4_snapshot_00.11.422.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Now a text prompt is all it takes to generate reality-warping images using Google Earth's satellite, aerial, and 3D imagery, like these images generated by [_Digital Digging_](https://www.digitaldigging.org/p/how-to-plant-a-nuclear-plant-in-iran)_'s_ Henk van Ess that show "refugees near the Mexican border" and a bomb crater near a hospital in Gaza.

Google [responded](https://x.com/NewsFromGoogle/status/2083024627761082702?s=20) to _Digital Digging_'s AI-altered images, saying, "We take misinformation seriously - every image created with Nano Banana in Google Earth includes the SynthID digital watermark, so if someone is unsure about an image, they can ask the Gemini app or use Lens in Search to see if the image was AI-generated." title: (No AI) The major labels propose rules to keep AI slop off the charts
author: Terrence O’Brien
content:
![Image showing a cartoony robot head with music notes inside a speech bubble near it.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/05/STK467_AI_Music.webp?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Several record labels, including the big three - Universal Music Group, Sony Music, and Warner Music Group - have proposed rules regarding [chart eligibility for AI songs](https://www.sonymusic.com/sony-music-corporate-non-home/believe-bmg-concord-dirty-hit-glassnote-records-hybe-mompop-music-partisan-records-sony-music-universal-music-group-and-warner-music-group-set-out-proposal-for-global-principles-for-eligibil/). In short, [they wouldn't be](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/music/music-industry-news/record-labels-call-to-disqualify-ai-slop-songs-from-charts-1236659042/).

The proposal goes quite a bit further than a [labeling proposal](https://www.riaa.com/music-community-introduces-new-labeling-programto-distinguish-generative-ai-in-sound-recordings/) put forth by the RIAA, the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI), SAG-AFTRA, and others. That would create a set of standardized labels for AI-generated and AI-assisted music. The labels' proposal would require songs be clearly labeled, but it would also keep them off international charts unless they met specific criteria, including being "substantially human …
